authority.rule: Mission-specific checkpoints are evidence only. They may not redefine the project-wide mission or bypass this control state.

active_mission.objective: Fix the overall Operation Pancake decision-making process so every consequential project decision follows MAP -> HISTORY -> RESEARCH -> CAPABILITIES -> PLAN -> EXECUTE -> ADAPT -> VERIFY -> UPDATE MAP -> CONTINUE across chats, tools, failures, handoffs, and future features.

acceptance_criteria.description: One project-wide authoritative control state exists and mission-specific state is subordinate.
MAP/HISTORY/RESEARCH/CAPABILITIES are evidence-backed prerequisites before consequential planning or execution.
Failures are classified without silently replacing the active mission, and capability failures drive ADAPT.
Accepted and rejected approaches cannot be reopened without materially new evidence.
BLOCKED is allowed only for a genuine external dependency after capabilities and adaptations are exhausted.
A deterministic handoff is generated from the authoritative state and detects stale mission/revision/next-action data.
Protected CI validates the project-wide control state and its regression suite before persistent repository changes.
Known Operation Pancake failures are encoded as regression tests and failure-audit controls.
A fresh-session simulation can recover mission, locks, capabilities, and next action from the authority alone.
The process continues after checkpoints while executable work remains and does not require the user to say next.

The existing repository SOP validator already enforces evidence-backed stages for Git changes but is mission-specific and lacks project-wide mission/lock/handoff/blocker semantics.

A project-wide source of truth plus deterministic preflight/handoff validation can make repository/Codex work durable while remaining honest that ordinary ChatGPT still depends on consulting that source.

Files/Library provides authoritative historical checkpoints across prior chats.

No authorized direct Windows shell/process channel is assumed in this chat.
Opera is a browser capability only and must never be treated as the project mission or sole decision-control mechanism.
